source: Owner message on 2026-10-10 to the Claude Code session doing AskRigor work, after it moved the AskRigor owner questions page into a Markdown file in Git and the page lost its colours.
owner_statement: you need to fix the owwner questions page, it used to be color coded so i could see what was questions vs todo, and what was done
problem: The published artifact showed each item's state with coloured labels: green for done, amber for to do, blue for next. Converting the page to a Markdown file in Git, as patterns/cross-account-continuity.md requires, kept the words but lost the colours, so the owner could no longer tell questions, to-dos and finished items apart at a glance.
required_behavior: Every item on an owner questions page shows by colour whether it is a question for the owner, something for him to do, next or in progress, or done or decided, with the same colours throughout and a one-line legend under the header.
In a Git file, the colours use what the host renders: on GitHub, a coloured callout under each section heading and a coloured marker at the start of each item's heading.
A published view keeps the same colours.
basis: The original AskRigor page's colour classes: done green, to do amber, next blue.
scope: Rule 9 and the status note of patterns/owner-questions-page.md, this record, and their tests.

origin.owner_outcome: The owner sees at a glance what is a question, what is for him to do, and what is done.
origin.notes: The GitHub callout types and marker colours are the assistant's choice of mechanism; purple marks a question because the original page had no open question to copy a colour from.

execution_surfaces.surface: patterns/owner-questions-page.md, reached through LESSON-INDEX.md and docs/INDEX.md

execution_surfaces.note: Colour-coded on 2026-10-10 by the requesting session; GitHub's renderer was checked to produce the callouts.

execution_surfaces.reason: Each workstream's own session applies the colours when it next updates its page.

nonclaims: Colours help only where the reader's GitHub view renders callouts and emoji; the status word stays in every heading, so the meaning survives without colour.
No repository rule can force a session that never loaded UDA.
